display.title: At Home Everything Is Different: The Maggid's Real Home
display.summary_short: The Baal Shem Tov sends Reb Chaim with a letter to the Maggid of Mezritch, who lives in a bare cabin and explains that his real home, in Gan Eden, is furnished with Torah and mitzvos.
display.summary_long: A Chassidic story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. The Baal Shem Tov often sends his Chassid Reb Chaim to help Jews in nearby towns, and one day gives him a sealed letter for his outstanding student, Reb Ber, later known as the Maggid of Mezritch. Reb Chaim expects a fine house, but finds the shabbiest cabin in town, with cracked windows, logs for chairs and a plank that serves as table by day and bed by night. The Maggid finishes teaching his students, stands up in honor of his Rebbe's letter, and serves his guest a meal. When Reb Chaim asks why he has no furniture, the Maggid answers in Yiddish, 'At home it is altogether different.' This world is only a temporary lodging; the soul's real home is in Gan Eden, and Hashem sends us down here to 'go shopping' for its furnishings, which are the Torah we learn and the mitzvos we do. Reb Chaim never forgets the lesson: do your shopping now, while you are alive, by learning more Torah and doing more mitzvos.
display.lesson: This world is a temporary home; put your effort into Torah and mitzvos, which furnish the soul's eternal home.
